title: Dependencies, installs, and exported targets
summary: Find a package, link its imported target, and install an exported target set.

scenario.briefing: The campus report links a system copy of fmt by absolute path, so it breaks on other machines. Find the package, link the imported target, and install the library with an export others can consume.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Review an artifact and identify the concrete risks.

hints: find_package(fmt 10 REQUIRED) defines the imported target fmt::fmt.
Link fmt::fmt and Threads::Threads with target_link_libraries, not archive paths.
Guard source include paths with BUILD_INTERFACE and install paths with INSTALL_INTERFACE.
Export report_core with install(TARGETS ... EXPORT ...) and install(EXPORT ...).

misconceptions.feedback: An absolute archive path encodes one machine's layout. find_package plus the imported target resolves the library and its requirements per environment.

misconceptions.description: Using include_directories to make headers visible.
misconceptions.feedback: Global include paths leak to every target and hide ownership. target_include_directories keeps the path on the target that needs it.

sections.title: Packages describe themselves
sections.body: find_package locates a dependency through its config file and defines imported targets. fmt::fmt carries the include directories, compile definitions, and link libraries the dependency needs, so the build does not guess paths.

sections.title: Installing is exporting a contract
sections.body: install(TARGETS ... EXPORT ...) records targets in an export set, and install(EXPORT ...) writes a package file that other projects can consume with find_package. Out-of-source builds keep generated files separate from the source tree.

vocabulary.definition: A target created by find_package that carries a dependency's usage requirements.
A named collection of installable targets that CMake turns into a package file.
A build whose generated files live in a directory separate from the source tree.

steps.title: Consume and export a CMake package
steps.prompt: Edit CMakeLists.txt. Find fmt and Threads, link them to report_core, install the library and executable, and export the library target set.

files.content:
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)
project(campus_report LANGUAGES CXX)

# TODO: find fmt and Threads and link them through their imported targets
add_library(report_core STATIC src/report.cpp)
target_include_directories(report_core PUBLIC /usr/local/include)
target_link_libraries(report_core PRIVATE /usr/local/lib/libfmt.a)

add_executable(report src/main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(report PRIVATE report_core)

include_directories(include)

tests.description: fmt and Threads are found as packages.
The library links imported targets, not archive paths.
The install exports report_core for other projects.
The build is configured out of source.

steps.title: Review the dependency wiring
steps.prompt: Review the CMake build file and select every real problem.

artifact.title: CMakeLists.txt
artifact.caption: The build hardcodes absolute paths and applies includes globally instead of using the imported package target.
artifact.content:
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)
project(campus_report LANGUAGES CXX)

include_directories(/home/ada/campus/include)
include_directories(include)

find_package(fmt REQUIRED)
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS "-I/usr/local/include")

add_executable(report src/main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(report fmt::fmt)

add_executable(copy src/copy.cpp)
target_link_libraries(copy fmt::fmt)

install(TARGETS report DESTINATION bin)

findings.label: The build hardcodes /home/ada/campus/include instead of using a target include directory.
include_directories applies paths to every target in the directory.
fmt is linked through its imported fmt::fmt target.
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS "-I/usr/local/include") smuggles another absolute include path past the target model.

verdicts.label: Block the change until the hardcoded paths and global includes are replaced.
Ship it; absolute paths are portable enough.
Only naming and formatting need work.

steps.explanation: The build reaches outside the project with /home/ada and /usr/local, applies include paths to every target, and bypasses the fmt imported target's requirements. It cannot configure on another machine. Dependency paths must come from find_package, and install rules must export targets.
